_comment: Strings that i18n-scan finds but that must NOT be translated.
Two kinds live here, and the distinction matters:
ignoreFiles — whole files whose string literals are addressed to a machine
or are proper nouns (model ids, provider names, LLM tool
schemas). Translating any of them changes behaviour rather
allow       — individual proper nouns sitting in files that DO also hold
real UI text, so the file itself cannot be skipped.
Adding an entry here is a claim that a human looked and decided. Do not add
a string just to make the scan quieter.

src/shared/heroPayload.ts is only the offline fallback for hero.json, which is fetched from the release server in English. Translating the fallback alone would switch the card's language with network state.
AiEnginesSettings CLI hints are kept English by the author's documented decision (technical data).
Strings starting "Automated guardrail" (src/main/index.ts) and the voice-orchestrator heads-up (src/main/realtimeActions.ts) are messages injected into agent sessions, not UI.
The webhook detail string is an API contract, not UI copy.
"Stanley" is the example name in the agent-name placeholder, not UI copy.
allow: http://localhost:11434/v1 (Ollama) — injected as a local provider
OpenAI-compatible endpoint — used as the proxy upstream
local models are file-based (models.json); base-URL reserved
Automated guardrail: {…}. Re-check your approach — if you're looping or stuck, STOP repeating, summarize what you've tried, and ask god for direction.
Automated guardrail escalated: {…}. Stop active work now: switch to read-only/plan, write a short plan of your next step, and send it to god for sign-off BEFORE running more tools.
{…} (voice orchestrator, {…}) just did: {…} on {…}{…}. Heads-up so we don't duplicate — the board is the single source of truth.
accepted — waiting for the operator to approve it before the hive sees it
